Geometric Jacobians

Source: R/jacobians.R
robot_jacobian.Rd

Returns the 6 by n geometric Jacobian of frame, mapping joint velocities to the spatial velocity of the frame. Rows are ordered linear first, \((v_x, v_y, v_z, \omega_x, \omega_y, \omega_z)\), and columns follow the configuration order of robot_joint_names(). Columns of joints that do not move the frame are zero.

robot_jacobian(
  robot,
  q,
  frame = NULL,
  reference = c("world", "local", "space"),
  point = NULL
)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model.

q

Configuration.

frame

Frame name (NULL for the end effector).

reference

"world", "local", or "space".

point

Optional point offset in the frame coordinates, for the Jacobian of a point fixed to the frame.

Value

A 6 by n matrix.

Details

The reference argument fixes the coordinates:

  • "world" (default): \(v\) is the velocity of the frame origin (or point) and \(\omega\) the angular velocity, both expressed in world coordinates. This is the Jacobian used for inverse kinematics.

  • "local": the same velocities expressed in the axes of frame (the body Jacobian).

  • "space": the spatial twist, whose linear part is the velocity of the body point that instantaneously coincides with the world origin (the space Jacobian of Lynch and Park).

For a revolute joint with world axis \(z\) through point \(o\), the world column is \((z \times (p - o), z)\); for a prismatic joint it is \((z, 0)\). The geometric Jacobian gives angular velocities; it is not the derivative of Euler angles, which is given by robot_jacobian_analytic().

Examples

robot <- robot_example("planar2")
robot_jacobian(robot, c(0.2, 0.4))[1:2, ]
#>        joint1     joint2
#> vx -0.7633118 -0.5646425
#> vy  1.8054022  0.8253356
